Join each full segment to the minimal segment it was cut from

Source: R/lnk_streams_parent.R
lnk_streams_parent.Rd

Builds <schema>.streams_parent for one watershed group: for every segment of the full network (schema, for example fresh_default) the segment of the minimal network (schema_minimal, for example fresh_default_minimal) it lies in, with that segment's gradient and length. A habitat rule tuned on the minimal network can then read the gradient it was tuned on at each full segment.

Usage

lnk_streams_parent(
  conn,
  wsg,
  schema,
  schema_minimal,
  tol_m = 1.01,
  sliver_m = 0.01,
  cut_floor_m = 0.5,
  run_id_full = NULL,
  run_id_minimal = NULL
)

Arguments

conn

A DBI::DBIConnection to the database holding both persist schemas.

wsg

Character. One watershed group code.

schema

Character. The full network's persist schema; the table is written there.

schema_minimal

Character. The minimal network's persist schema.

tol_m

Numeric. How far, in metres, a minimal cut may lie from the nearest full cut.

sliver_m

Numeric. Overlap pieces shorter than this, in metres, are dropped.

cut_floor_m

Numeric. A minimal segment starting above this measure is a cut; one starting at or below it starts its line.

run_id_full, run_id_minimal

Character or NULL. When given, the log.run_id of the build a caller judged on each side; the join is refused if the group's newest build is another one (it was re-modelled after the judgement).

Value

A one-row data frame, invisibly: wsg, n_full, n_minimal, km, n_straddle (full segments with straddle_m of sliver_m or more), km_straddle, max_straddle_m.

Details

Segments are matched by measure overlap on each blue_line_key, never by id_segment (each build numbers its own). Pieces shorter than sliver_m are dropped (an FWA segment's upstream measure can overshoot the next one's start by a few millimetres), and each full segment takes the minimal segment it overlaps most. The join is refused unless every minimal cut above cut_floor_m on its line has a full cut within tol_m of it, so a full segment straddles a minimal cut by at most about tol_m; the full build skips a cut within 1 m of an existing end. It is also refused when the pieces do not cover both networks' km, or when a full segment would get no row.

The group's rows are replaced in one transaction, so a refusal leaves its earlier rows in place. Nothing on the modelling path reads or writes the table: a re-model of either network leaves its rows behind, and run_id_full, run_id_minimal and overlap_m + straddle_m (the full segment's length) are what tell a stale row. Whether the two builds ran the same modelling code is judged by the caller (data-raw/streams_parent_build.R).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- lnk_db_conn(dbname = "fwapg", host = "localhost", port = 5432L,
                    user = "postgres", password = "postgres")
lnk_streams_parent(conn, "BULK", schema = "fresh_default",
                   schema_minimal = "fresh_default_minimal")
DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
  SELECT s.id_segment, s.gradient, p.gradient_minimal, p.straddle_m
    FROM fresh_default.streams s
    JOIN fresh_default.streams_parent p USING (id_segment, watershed_group_code)
   WHERE s.watershed_group_code = 'BULK' LIMIT 5")
} # }
